Incident Bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: p0 - spike in user-reported hallucinations / quality drop. Auto-detected signal from quality-guard on prod (nlp-quality). Potential culprit: econ-routing (cost-led fallback) sending traffic to economy-v1-q4. Alerting on-call. https://dash.redwood/internal/alerts/2145678901
Alex P.: on it. I'm oncall for eng-runtime. Pulling routing logs now.
Samir G.: thx alex. I can look at policy engine while you pull logs.
Maria L.: Support getting multiple customer tickets — some enterprise customers seeing incorrect factual output and hallucinations. ETA to mitigation?
Alex P.: looking at router traces. I see a surge of traffic re-routed to economy-v1-q4 at 21:11 UTC. Policy eval shows cost_score beating quality_score due to a mis-evaluated policy weight. snippet: ```policy_eval: {cost_weight: 1.2, quality_weight: 0.8, final_score: 0.72} -> selected variant: economy-v1-q4```
Jess T.: I just checked the rollout config. There was a recent change to policy defaults in canary that accidentally propagated globally: `routes.default.cost_weight=1.2` (should be 0.6). PR #4953 merged this morning.
Elena R.: oh no. That explains it. The canary was supposed to be scoped to dev only.
Samir G.: Confirming a region fallback loop too. When economy-v1-q4 hits rate limits in eu-west, requests fall back to cheaper variants in other regions -> more cheap traffic. Looks like `allow_cross_region_economy: true` combined with the bad weight.
Alex P.: immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable cost-led routing policy globally, 2) pin affected customers to stable variants, 3) rollback PR or patch weights, 4) notify customers. Who can make the global toggle? @Kyle H.?
Kyle H.: I can flip the toggle. Doing step 1 now. /ops toggle econ-routing.enabled false
Incident Bot: Action recorded: econ-routing.enabled set -> false by Kyle H. at 21:13:04 UTC.
Support Bot: Notifying affected customers (list from alerts): Acme Corp, Finly, PaperTrail. Draft sent: "We're investigating increased hallucinations; routing policy temporarily disabled. More updates soon."
Jess T.: creating hotfix to revert default weight to 0.6 and add canary scope guard. Patch: ```routes.default.cost_weight=0.6; routes.canary.scope=dev-only``` pushing now.
Samir G.: pinning high-tier enterprise customers to `stable-v2` variant while we validate. Running: ```route pin --customer=acme --variant=stable-v2 --until=2026-03-15T23:00Z```
Alex P.: reviewing logs after toggle. Early signs: traffic moving back to stable variants, error-rate for stable models is back to baseline. Need to verify quality metrics (BLEU / factuality proxy) are recovering.
Maria L.: customers on calls asking for RCA — we'll need ETA for rollback and full recovery. Kyle, can you also mute any automated scaling/burst that would re-enable economy variants?
Kyle H.: done. `autoscale.burst.economy=false` and put a guard on region fallback: `allow_cross_region_economy=false`.
Incident Bot: diagnostics snapshot attached: https://dash.redwood/internal/snapshots/2145678901 - contains routing trace, alert graph, and sample queries.
Jess T.: hotfix merged and deployed to control plane at 21:18 UTC. Canary run shows no immediate regressions. Rolling rollout to prod with 5% check.
Alex P.: running quality smoke tests against a saved prompt set (regression-suite v2). Results in progress...
Samir G.: observed a small queue of requests that previously dropped into econ variant; replaying them against stable to confirm outputs. Quick diff shows hallucination rate down from 4.1% -> 0.7% on sample batch.
Elena R.: coordinating with SRE to monitor latency — pinning stable increases cost a bit but restores quality. Relevant dashboard: https://dash.redwood/internal/dashboards/routing-econ-impact
Maria L.: customer comms: initial message sent. Next update planned in 30m with mitigation summary and ETA for full RCA.
Kyle H.: handing off to next oncall (Elena) in 15m. Elena, you have the war room. I'll stay on the thread for context.
Elena R.: taking over. I'll keep an eye on the canary and escalate if quality metrics don't stabilize by 21:40 UTC. Setting up a short-lived watch: `watch quality: 60s`
Support Bot: Logged support tickets for follow-up and created damage-assessment doc (internal link).
Alex P.: notes for postmortem: root cause = accidental global propagation of canary config (cost_weight change) + missing scope guard + no hard cap on cross-region economy fallback. Contributing factor = recent PR lacked a QA check for policy defaults.
Jess T.: post-deploy actions: add CI check that forbids default policy changes without a feature flag; add test that simulates cost/quality weights and ensures stability.
Samir G.: ops action: implement a hard upper-bound on cost_weight (<=1.0) and a canary-scoping enforcement in control plane.
Elena R.: current state at 21:22 UTC: canary traffic 5% -> stable, sample quality metrics within acceptable range, no new customer complaints in last 8 min. Continuing monitoring.
Maria L.: thanks team. We'll prep a customer-facing summary and a follow-up internal RCA. I'll schedule the postmortem for tomorrow and assign owners.
Kyle H.: quick reminder in thread: please include timeline, alert graphs, PR numbers (#4953), commands run, and list of affected accounts in the postmortem.
Alex P.: agreed. I'll draft the timeline starting with the alert at 21:11 UTC.
Incident Bot: SESSION CLOSED (automated) - incident downgraded to sev-2 at 21:32 UTC after stabilization.
Elena R.: leaving follow-up tasks: (1) rollback any remaining dev-propagated defaults, (2) implement guardrails, (3) customer RCA. Assigning to Jess, Samir, Maria respectively.
Support Bot: customers updated with mitigation and estimated RCA delivery time.
Alex P.: thanks all. Postmortem to be posted to #postmortems and linked from the customer update."
